issues.failure_explanation: The two displayed cases are not exhaustive. For example, if \tilde{u}_h^+=-5, \tilde{u}_h^-=-6 and u_{\theta^*}=4, then |u_{\theta^*}| is not larger than max{|\tilde{u}_h^+|,|\tilde{u}_h^-|} and u_{\theta^*} is not between \tilde{u}_h^- and \tilde{u}_h^+, yet the sign is constant across the interface. The proof gives no bound for this remaining case, so the jump-term estimate used in the stability argument is incomplete.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first case by the standard exhaustive condition u_{\theta^*} > max{\tilde{u}_h^+,\tilde{u}_h^-} or u_{\theta^*} < min{\tilde{u}_h^+,\tilde{u}_h^-}; the already-written sign-constant bound then covers all remaining cases.
issues.overall_effect: The interface jump bounds in the single-shock proof, and every later result that explicitly reuses eq:estimate_jump or eq:estimate_jump_2, are not fully justified as written.
issues.title: Incomplete sign case split in the single-shock jump estimate
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line correction of the case split and preserves all claimed rates and scope; no new construction or global argument is needed.

Let $u$ be the entropy solution of \eqref{eq:scalar-HCL} satisfying Assumption~\ref{assump:shock_3d}.

issues.failure_explanation: The 1D statement treats a shock interaction at the terminal time T, but the cited multi-D theorem and Assumption shoc_3d are formulated for compact shock hypersurfaces inside the open space-time domain Ω_T and for interior transversal codimension-two intersections. The proof of thm:more_general_case also excises an interior tubular neighborhood of Σ and does not address an interaction located on the final-time boundary. Hence the reference does not establish the special case claimed.

failure_location.quote: A complete argument is contained in the proof of the more general higher-dimensional interaction result, Theorem~\ref{thm:more_general_case}; the present statement is a special case of that theorem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a self-contained 1D terminal-interaction argument or extend the multi-D assumption and proof to cover interactions at t=T; at minimum, the special-case claim must be justified rather than delegated to an inapplicable theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The stated O(h^{1/2}) convergence for terminal-time shock interactions is unsupported, and the global 1D theorem that patches this local result is affected.
issues.title: Shock-interaction theorem cited from an inapplicable multi-D result
issues.why_classification: A contained local 1D boundary-interaction proof, or a boundary extension of the existing argument, can preserve the stated rate; it is nontrivial, so the issue is not minor, but it does not require new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs the log-integrable singular bound in the moving coordinate \hat x=x-x_q-a_q(t-\tau_q), with |t-\tau_q|^3. Assumption (iv) as written uses (t-\tau_q)^3+(x-x_q)^2, i.e. it is centered at the birth point rather than at the shock curve and does not use absolute time for the pre-birth side. For a_q\neq0 this does not imply the stated G(\hat t,\hat x) bound, so the integral estimate leading to |ln h| is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct Assumption (iv) to the standard moving-coordinate nondegenerate shock-birth bound, e.g. in terms of |t-\tau_q|^3+(x-\gamma_q^b(t)-x_q)^2 or x-\gamma_q^b(t), or add the required pre/post-birth estimates; the existing proof then proceeds.
issues.overall_effect: The smooth-initial-data shock-formation theorem, and the 1D main theorem in the presence of shock-birth pieces, are not established as written.
issues.title: Shock-birth proof uses a bound not supplied by Assumption (iv)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of the hypothesis/coordinate used in the proof and preserves the claimed rate; it does not require a new argument or loss of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Proceeding as in Step~5 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:shock}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only establishes the total residual bound ∫_{Ω_T}|∇·F(u_{θ*})|≲1, but it asserts that the residual over each O(h^{1/2})-wide interface region Ω_i is ≲h^{1/2}. In 1D this follows from a strip-selection/averaging argument; in the multi-D setting with several shock hypersurfaces and a codimension-two intersection set, no such selection argument is given. Without it, the I1 estimate and the final O(h^{1/2}) conclusion do not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a finite-dimensional averaging/selection argument showing ∫_{Ω_i}|∇·F(u_{θ*})|≲h^{1/2} for the finitely many shifted interface regions, or weaken the theorem's rate or assumptions; at minimum, the asserted local residual bound must be proved.
issues.overall_effect: The multi-D convergence theorem for multiple shock hypersurfaces is unsupported, and any result relying on that theorem as a complete argument, notably the 1D shock-interaction theorem, is affected.
issues.title: Multi-D multiple-shock theorem lacks a residual selection for interface regions
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a contained local selection estimate analogous to the 1D argument; supplying it can preserve the h^{1/2} rate without abandoning the multi-D strategy, but it is nontrivial and absent.
